images.caption: Eastbourne Pier appears in the Agatha Christie's Poirot episode "Jewel Robbery at the Grand Metropolitan" (although ostensibly, the story is located in Brighton) and in "Curtain: Poirot's Last Case". It was also featured in the 2001 film Last Orders and the 2008 film Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging. The 2010 film Brighton Rock used Eastbourne Pier to stand in for Brighton's Palace Pier.

images.caption:
Restaurants by Sovereign Harbour
Sovereign Harbour is a large development of beach-lands on the outskirts of Eastbourne, East Sussex, that began construction in 1991.
The development , includes a harbour, 24 hour marinas, business park, shops and restaurants, and over 3000 houses, apartments, flats and townhouses; including holiday properties.

Entering the marina from the sea through the outer marina by two sea locks leads you to the inner marina and off that three further marinas, south marina, west marina and north marina.

images.caption:
Bateman's was built around 1634. Rudyard Kipling bought Bateman's in 1902. He and his American wife, Carrie, had discovered the house two years earlier but had been too slow in deciding to buy it and it was let before they could close the deal. When the house came on the market again in 1902, they had no hesitation and bought it along with the surrounding buildings, the mill and 33 acres for £9,300. It had no bathroom, no running water upstairs and no electricity but Kipling loved it. Rudyard Kipling died in 1936 and Carrie continued to live at Bateman's until her death in 1939.

I won a wineglass on eBay to replace one that was broken. The seller lives just off my route to visit my mother. Near his house I saw a sign to Bateman's. It was closed. I must go back whan it is open...
